home.title: Centrifugal Pump Knowledge Base
home.lede: A working reference for engineers who specify, inspect, commission, operate and overhaul centrifugal pumps — covering hydraulics, construction, rotor forces, selection, testing, installation, maintenance and field troubleshooting.

pages.title: Pump Fundamentals and Classification
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Core reference › Fundamentals
pages.lede: How pumps are classified, where the centrifugal machine sits among them, the construction families you will meet on a plant, and the design standards that govern them.

pages.title: Design and Construction
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Core reference › Construction
pages.lede: The parts that decide how a pump performs and how long it lasts: impellers, casings and diffusers, wear rings, shafts and sleeves, packing, mechanical seals, bearing housings and couplings.

pages.title: Pump Hydraulics, Cavitation and NPSH
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Core reference › Hydraulics
pages.lede: The quantitative core of pump engineering — head, flow and system resistance, efficiency and power, the characteristic curve and its corrections, specific speed, and the cavitation, recirculation and NPSH behaviour that destroys more impellers than anything else.

pages.title: Forces in Centrifugal Pumps
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Core reference › Forces
pages.lede: Axial thrust and radial load — where they come from, how each impeller and casing arrangement manages them, and how shaft deflection translates them into seal and bearing failures.

pages.title: Operation and Characteristic Curves
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Core reference › Operation
pages.lede: Reading and using the four characteristic curves: curve stability and steepness, why the H–Q and P–Q curves take the shape they do, parallel and series operation, speed–torque at start-up, flow regulation, and the limits of the allowable operating region.

pages.title: Specification and Selection
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Project lifecycle › Selection
pages.lede: System analysis through to award: establishing boundary conditions and flow requirements, specifying the fluid and the criticality, writing the data sheet, issuing the bid request and scoring the bids.

pages.title: Testing and Inspection
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Project lifecycle › Testing
pages.lede: Holding the vendor to the data sheet: material and casting inspection, NDE methods and acceptance codes, hydrostatic and shop performance tests, tolerance tables, the NPSH test, and what to do when a test fails.

pages.title: Installation and Commissioning
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Project lifecycle › Installation
pages.lede: Siting, foundation design, grouting, alignment, suction and discharge piping rules, pre-operational checks and the start-up sequence — the stage where most of a pump's service life is won or lost.

pages.title: Maintenance and Reliability
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Project lifecycle › Maintenance
pages.lede: Condition monitoring and overhaul: the four-pillar predictive programme, failure diagnosis before strip-down, the dimensional checks that matter, reassembly of single-stage, vertical and multistage pumps, and the economics of when to overhaul.

pages.title: Field Troubleshooting Guide
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Field tools › Troubleshooting
pages.lede: Sixteen symptoms an operator or technician actually reports, each with its credible cause list and the checks that discriminate between them. Filter by symptom group or search the full text.

pages.title: Engineering Calculators
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Field tools › Calculators
pages.lede: Six calculations engineers reach for constantly — NPSH available and margin, affinity-law scaling, specific and suction specific speed, power and motor sizing, low-flow temperature rise, and system head. All run in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.

pages.title: Formula and Data Sheet
pages.crumbs: Knowledge base › Field tools › Formulas
pages.lede: Every equation, limit, clearance and tolerance in this knowledge base on one page, with units stated. Formatted to print cleanly for a site folder or a toolbox.

pages.title: Glossary of Pump Terminology
pages.lede: The vocabulary used across the knowledge base, defined for engineers who need the working meaning rather than the textbook derivation.

pages.title: Standards, Sources and Scope
pages.lede: Which standard governs which decision, how to choose between API, ANSI/ASME and ISO for a given service, the sources this knowledge base draws on, and an honest statement of what it does and does not cover.
